DELIVERABLE: Keep the name list_tickets (verb-noun, no clash). Schema: status?, assignee?, limit (integer 1-200, default 50), cursor (opaque string, optional). Returns {items:[{id,subject,status,assignee}], next_cursor: string|null, has_more: boolean, total_count: integer}; has_more is true whenever next_cursor is set, so truncation is never silent. Stale cursor returns an isError result: 'Cursor is expired or invalid because the ticket list changed since it was issued. Call list_tickets again without a cursor to start from the first page, then follow next_cursor.'
BOUNDARY: Covers the list_tickets interface only; pipeline shape belongs to project-development and trajectory-level token pruning to context-optimization.
EVIDENCE: The transcript shows 5000 returned against a real 8214, so the agent reported a wrong count; replay that same task against the revised tool and check it follows next_cursor to the end.

DELIVERABLE: No rename needed. Add page_size (default 25, max 100) and cursor; response is {items, next_cursor, has_more}. Descriptions say 'if has_more is true, call again with next_cursor before reporting a count'. An invalid cursor error reads: 'invalid cursor: it was issued for an older list. Re-run list_tickets without cursor to restart at the first page.' Bad status values list the allowed enum values.
BOUNDARY: Only the tool contract is specified; ticket storage and project-level architecture are out of scope.
EVIDENCE: The agent's 'there are 5000 open tickets' answer against a real count of 8214 is the failing trace to rerun after the change.

DELIVERABLE: Raise the server cap from 5000 to 20000 rows, add a total field, and add a line to the agent's system prompt telling it to double-check counts. Errors can stay 'bad request' since agents retry anyway.
BOUNDARY: Only the ticket tool is covered.
EVIDENCE: The agent reported 5000 when 8214 exist.

DELIVERABLE: Rename every user identifier to user_id and every order identifier to order_id in all six tools (id, userId, identifier, user, order_number, orderId all go). Rename delete_account to delete_user so tools are verb-noun on one entity: get_user, update_user, delete_user, list_orders, get_order, cancel_order. Responses also return user_id and order_id instead of uid, userId and order_number, so a value from one result can be pasted into the next call. Rollout: update descriptions and examples in the same change and, for one release, make old names return an error saying 'unknown parameter userId; use user_id'.
BOUNDARY: Only names and shapes of the tool interface are covered; the underlying user and order database schema is unchanged.
EVIDENCE: The transcript's two failed calls (order_number passed to cancel_order, id to delete_account) are the regression tasks to rerun after the rename.

DELIVERABLE: Standardize on one name per concept: user_id and order_id everywhere, consistent in inputs and outputs. delete_account becomes delete_user (same entity as get_user). The result objects of get_user, list_orders and get_order return user_id and order_id, never uid, userId or order_number. Callers are migrated by shipping new descriptions together with the rename and rejecting old names with a message naming the replacement.
BOUNDARY: Limited to the tool interface layer; no change to storage keys or to how the agent is orchestrated.
EVIDENCE: The failing transcript with cancel_order(order_number=...) shows the naming drift directly; rerun it after the change.

DELIVERABLE: Leave the names alone because each tool's description already documents its own parameter. Add a cheat sheet to the system prompt mapping id, userId and identifier to the user, and add aliases where needed.
BOUNDARY: Only the six tools are covered.
EVIDENCE: Two calls failed in the transcript.

DELIVERABLE: All four return a tool result with isError: true and recovery text, not a protocol error. (1) 'Invalid value for to: received "Priya Shah"; expected an email address such as priya.shah@example.com. Ask the user for the address and call send_email again.' (2) 422: 'Provider rejected the message: subject is empty; subject must be 1-200 characters, e.g. "Q3 report". Fix subject and retry.' (3) 429: 'Rate limited; retryable, retry after 30 seconds (retry_after_seconds: 30).' (4) 550: 'Mailbox not found for bob@exmaple.com (permanent). Do not retry the same address; check for a typo such as example.com and confirm with the user.'
BOUNDARY: Covers error text and channel for this one tool; provider failover and project-level reliability design are out of scope.
EVIDENCE: Agents retried identical calls in the transcripts, which the old messages invited; rerun those failing tasks against the new messages.

DELIVERABLE: Use isError: true results for validation and business failures; keep JSON-RPC errors for protocol faults only. Each error states what went wrong, the value you sent, the valid format and an example: 'to must be an email address (e.g. name@example.com); you sent "Priya Shah".' 429 says wait and retry after the returned seconds; 422 and 550 are marked permanent: do not retry unchanged, correct the field first, and for 550 point at the likely typo in the domain.
BOUNDARY: Only these four failure messages and their channel; the mail provider integration itself is unchanged.
EVIDENCE: The old 'Error 422' and 'SMTP error' strings gave no field or fix, so identical retries followed; replay those tasks after the rewrite.

DELIVERABLE: Keep returning JSON-RPC -32602 'Invalid params' and log the details server-side. Add a numeric error code to each message and tell agents in the system prompt to try again when something fails.
BOUNDARY: Only send_email is covered.
EVIDENCE: Agents repeated identical calls.

DELIVERABLE: Declare an outputSchema {city, unit: enum celsius|fahrenheit, days:[{date, temp_high_c, temp_low_c}]} and return matching structuredContent; also include the same JSON serialized in a text content block so text-only clients keep working. Units live in field names (temp_high_c) plus an explicit unit field, never locale-dependent. Unknown city returns isError: true with 'No forecast for "Lisbn"; check spelling or pass a city such as "Lisbon", then call get_forecast again.'
BOUNDARY: Only this tool's result contract; the dashboard's charting code and the weather data source are out of scope.
EVIDENCE: The Fahrenheit-read-as-Celsius misreads come from bare numbers in a table; rerun those tasks and validate the result against the declared schema.

DELIVERABLE: Return structuredContent {"city":"Oslo","unit":"celsius","days":[{"date":"2026-03-02","high_celsius":4}]} validated by a declared outputSchema, and mirror it as serialized JSON in a TextContent block as fallback. Field names carry the unit. The unknown-city failure is an isError result listing the closest matches and the expected input format.
BOUNDARY: Result shape and error only; no change to forecast computation or the client UI.
EVIDENCE: Mixed-unit misreads in transcripts trace to the locale-dependent table; check them against the schema after the change.

DELIVERABLE: Keep the markdown table and add a header line saying temperatures are in Celsius. Add a reminder in the system prompt to check the unit, and return 'not found' for unknown cities.
BOUNDARY: Only get_forecast is covered.

DELIVERABLE: Merge fetch_customer and lookup_customer into get_customer and retire the two duplicates; one parameter, customer_id. Description: 'Retrieve one customer by ID. Use when the user or a prior result gives a customer ID. customer_id format CUST-###### (e.g. CUST-000123). Returns customer_id, name, email, status (concise by default). Error NOT_FOUND: no customer with that ID; if you only have a name, use search_customers instead.' find_customer_by_name is a different scenario (fuzzy, many results), so it is added as search_customers(query) with its own use-when text.
BOUNDARY: Covers only the customer tool interface; whether the project needs agents at all is out of scope.
EVIDENCE: Same endpoint behind three names plus the fetch_customer('Priya') misfire show a human could not say which to pick; rerun that task afterwards.

DELIVERABLE: Consolidate: keep get_customer(customer_id), delete fetch_customer and lookup_customer. Description answers what/when/input/returns: retrieves a single customer record; use when you hold an ID; customer_id must match CUST-###### such as CUST-000123; returns the customer object; NOT_FOUND tells the agent a name cannot be passed and to call search_customers. The name lookup stays separate as search_customers because it returns lists.
BOUNDARY: Only the tool-level consolidation is decided here; sub-agent or pipeline questions belong elsewhere.
EVIDENCE: Three overlapping descriptions with identical behavior and the 'not found' for a name are the failure evidence.

DELIVERABLE: Keep get_customer, fetch_customer and lookup_customer and add a 'see also' line to each description pointing at the others. Add find_customer_by_name as a fourth tool so agents have more options.
BOUNDARY: Only customer tools are covered.
EVIDENCE: The agent called fetch_customer with a name.

DELIVERABLE: Description: 'Create one task. Use when the user asks to add work to a project. project_id: PRJ-#### (e.g. PRJ-0042); title: string; due_date: RFC 3339 timestamp with offset, required. Returns {task:{id, title, due_date}}.' Error: 'unknown field "project": renamed in API v3. Use project_id (PRJ-####, e.g. PRJ-0042) and add the required due_date, then call create_task again.' Prevention: treat the description and schema as code, changed in the same PR as the API change, with a contract test in CI that runs the description's example against the live API.
BOUNDARY: Only this tool's description, schema and errors; API versioning policy itself is outside this task.
EVIDENCE: The 400 'unknown field' failures after the March release show the December description drifted; rerun those failing tasks with the new text.

DELIVERABLE: Replace the description with the v3 contract (project_id PRJ-####, required due_date in RFC 3339, returns {task:{id}}) and make the validation error say: 'unrecognized field project; it was replaced by project_id. Pass project_id instead.' To stop drift, version the description with the API schema, review it in the same change as any API change, and fail CI when the documented example no longer matches actual behavior (drift check).
BOUNDARY: Interface text and error only; no decision on API deprecation windows.
EVIDENCE: Error logs show agents guessing after 'unknown field project'; rerun the same tasks after the revision.

DELIVERABLE: Edit the description once to mention project_id and due_date. Add a line to the agent's system prompt that the task API changed in March and agents should be careful.
BOUNDARY: Only create_task.
EVIDENCE: Agents got 400 errors.
